problem: Thirteen subsetted fonts, none with a ToUnicode map, so every character extracts as a bare glyph index. EACH FONT IS ITS OWN CIPHER: the body face is 89% of the text and the sidebar/quote/table faces are separate substitutions. Decoding everything with the body font's mapping yields clean English for 89% and confident nonsense for the rest.
evidence: Solved by tools/solve_cid_bands.py, which anchors each font on English: the commonest 3-letter word gives the lowercase constant (cross-checked across all three of t/h/e), a capitalised word whose tail already decodes gives the uppercase one, and the two commonest word-final non-letters give the punctuation one as a SELF-CHECKING pair ('.' takes the lower cid, so 46+period must equal 44+comma). The solver independently reproduced the body font's 137/133/130, which had been derived by hand, and ZTR41C6's 130/124/119, which had been derived from a garbled sample the human spotted.
extractor: pdfplumber via tools/extract_born_digital.py --glyph-map. pdfplumber reports (cid:N) per character WITH its fontname, which is required here: poppler emits the raw glyph byte, losing the font attribution that tells you which cipher to apply — and additionally conflates glyph 32 with layout padding.

ZTR41D0.tmp,Bold.note: The entry-name / table-header display face — it draws the NAMES on the Wonders pages, which is why the artifact catalogue could not be authored past the eight entries that came off page images. Solved 2026-08-12 by crib, not by the band solver: the solver anchors on the commonest 3-letter word being 'the', and this face sets names and column headers where it is not. The cribs are the five magical-material run-in heads on core p.338 (Orichalcum:/Moonsilver:/Jade:/Starmetal:/Soulsteel:), which pin all 26 lowercase letters, nine capitals and the colon between them.
ZTR41D0.tmp,Bold.why_split_bands: This face is the reason `upper` and `punct` may be a LIST of [k, lo_ord, hi_ord] bands rather than one constant. A subset drops unused glyphs and every id after the gap shifts, so a face with a mid-alphabet gap needs two constants. Here 'Q' is not in the subset: A-P solve at 123 and R-Z at 124, proved by 'Poleaxe' (p.328) and 'Resources' (the weapon-table header) — decoding both with one constant turns one of them into 'Qoleaxe' or 'Sesources'. The punctuation splits the same way: ',' '-' '.' '/' 0-9 ':' at 118, and '(' ')' '*' at 117.

7.why: the RATING DOT in the display face — this is the glyph that carries 'Manse •••' after a Hearthstone name and the dot rating after an artifact name, so it is the one single-glyph mapping the catalogue work actually depends on. Read off the ten Hearthstones on core pp.338-340, whose ratings are stated again in their own body text.

ZTR41D0.tmp,Bold cids 4, 5, 6.note: Three glyphs of the otherwise-solved display face. 4 and 5 are a quote pair with ONE occurrence each in the whole book (p.13's 'over the top' pull-quote) and 6 is a separator ornament (77 uses: 'Familiar ? ', 'Step 1 ? Apply Bonuses:') that could be a bullet, an em dash or a diamond. Their band is not constrained by any crib, so they stay U+FFFD rather than get a plausible guess — none of them carries a game value.

ZTR41E6/DC/C8 and five tinier faces.note: UNSOLVED — too little text to anchor. Left as U+FFFD.

measured: 2026-08-11 after the per-font fix: 1,383,330 chars, 340 pages, 3.00% undecoded (the unsolved faces, every glyph marked U+FFFD). 337 of 340 pages read as English; the three that do not are the contents page, a creature stat table and the blank character sheet. 237 of 276 Core entries already authored FROM PAGE IMAGES are found, 188 of them on exactly their recorded page (up from 103 when a single font's mapping was applied to all thirteen).
